_comment_console: Where a human goes to look at a test. Taken from the Intelligems app's own link builder in its published bundle, not guessed: `e.category === 'experiment' ? r.pathname = '/experiment/' + e.id : r.pathname = '/personalization/' + e.id`. Verified 2026-09-11. The app also appends ?action=edit when opening its editor; that is deliberately omitted here, because these are links to look at a test, not to change one.
_VERIFIED: Endpoints, methods and response field names verified 2026-09-10 against the Intelligems External API reference AND against a real payload from the First Day Life Inc. account (org 86ab4ded-43f9-4a0a-a9ef-80dfd2b5508d, shop first-day-inc.myshopify.com). The captured payload is test/fixtures/intelligems-real.js and the collector is tested against it.

endpoints._comment: The analytics endpoints are POST, not GET, and take a JSON body. There is no /shop endpoint and no separate metrics-config endpoint: per-test key metrics ride on the experience object as experienceKeyMetrics. Pagination on /experiences-list is 1-BASED with a totalPages envelope, unlike ClickUp's 0-based paging.

categories._comment: Which experience categories are decisions. The live account returns two: 'experiment' and 'personalization'. A personalization is an always-on targeting rule with no control group, so a verdict, a readiness gate, a significance call and an audience breakdown are all meaningless for it, and each of those is an API call per run. They are set aside rather than dropped: the count and names ride on snapshot meta.setAside so the dashboard can account for them.

rateLimits._comment: Documented burst/refill: experience endpoints burst 50, refill 25 per 30s. Export burst 20. Sitewide burst 10, refill 5 per 30s. Response headers are x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset, where reset is MILLISECONDS UNTIL RESET, not an epoch. A 429 body carries retryAfter in seconds. A once-daily pull of 7 tests is nowhere near these limits.

readinessGate._comment: Confirmed against a live test: '[KCM-PDP] Price per Gummy' at 42 runtime_days with 254/238 orders per variant returns verdict not_ready. Days met, orders not, so not ready. 300 is per group. The platform returns runtime_days and orders_per_variant inside the testResult block, so the gate is read rather than recomputed, and any disagreement with our own arithmetic is flagged.

verdictMap._TODO: Alex to decide the mapping for the six actionable verdicts. The rest are not decisions. The spec listed six verdicts; the platform actually returns thirteen. 'error' means the verdict could not be computed. The six filtered_* variants are returned when filters were sent, and the platform documents that they describe a narrowed population rather than the full randomized group, so they must never be treated as wins or losses. This pipeline sends no filters, so filtered_* should never appear; they map to Keep Running so that a future filter cannot silently produce a Ship.

metrics._TODO: Alex to confirm. These are the real metric keys from the analytics response, not invented names, and they are drawn from what the live tests are actually configured on: conversionRate, netRevenuePerVisitor, profitPerVisitor, netRevenuePerOrder and addToCartRate. Two notes. There is no 'aov' key in the variation overview: AOV is net_revenue_per_order. And gross_profit_per_visitor is deliberately NOT in the P0 list because COGS is not configured on this account, so it returns null on every test.
metrics._comment: Per-test metrics are read automatically from the experience's experienceKeyMetrics and translated from camelCase to these snake_case keys. These lists are only the always-watch set on top of that.

p1Band._comment: A P1 metric is out of whack when it moves outside its own 95 percent interval day over day. The API returns ci_low and ci_high per metric. Metrics with a null interval, such as view_collection_page_rate on a low-traffic test, are SKIPPED and logged, never compared against zero.

postTest._comment: analyze view post_test returns customers who converted during the test, tracked by their purchase behavior afterwards, split by variation. With includeInTestOrders true the total_* family is the LTV view. This is the platform's own answer to the spec's future-value question and may remove the need for hand-entered LTV reference values entirely.

metricTree._comment: The cascading tree shown for each experiment. Two roots. RPV decomposes exactly into AOV x conversion rate, which is why `decomposes` is set on it: the children's contributions can be attributed to the parent's move. Nothing else in the tree is an identity, so nothing else claims attribution. Metric keys are the real snake_case keys the analytics response returns.

roots.label: RPV
roots.description: Revenue per visitor. The headline: it is the only metric that captures both how many visitors buy and how much they spend.

roots.label: Subscription share of orders
roots.description: The share of orders that are subscriptions. Separate root because it changes what a customer is WORTH, not what this order is worth, and the future-value projection is built on it.

audiences._comment: Audience breakdowns. Pulled during the daily run ONLY for tests past the readiness gate, and only on the dimensions listed here: it is one extra API call per test per dimension, and a test that cannot be called overall cannot be called by segment either. Other dimensions are available on demand from the dashboard.
audiences._comment_minOrders: The same per-group bar the readiness gate uses. A segment below it is reported as 'Too small', never as a result: slicing until something looks significant is the failure mode this whole feature invites, and the bar is the guard against it.
audiences._comment_dimensions: visitor_type first, because it is the only dimension on this store where BOTH segments clear the 300-order bar (New 1,345 and Returning 324 on a representative test), and because new versus returning is the split this business already reasons in. device_type is kept because it reliably shows Mobile as judgeable and Desktop as too small, which is itself worth knowing: this store is mobile-dominant enough that desktop cannot be called on a normal test. source_channel is available on demand but only Paid Social clears the bar, so pulling it every run would mostly produce 'Too small' rows.
